title: Salem's Lot (2024) - The amazing source material has to be filtered through uninspired filmmaking

commenti.body:
It's so bad, it makes the novel look bad. It makes the story seem so simple and dull. I mean, it is simple... But Stephen King knows how to tell a story. And the Tobe Hooper version is a little dull sometimes, but he brings a stark, visceral quality to the horror scenes. There's just nothing good in this new version. 

Like you said, this new version looks like a TV show. It's ironic, becuase the first one *was* a TV movie, but it was good enough to release theatrically overseas. This new one started out as a movie, but was released direct-to-stream because it's so bad.

> confirms his and James wan's creativity well has long dried up.

For next time, throwing these grandiose, trivial insults around at people doesn't do you any favors, OP. If you are trying to be taken seriously in your write-ups, keep the unnecessary and insulting commentary out and focus on the piece itself. Despite the last 10 or so years of childish politics making insulting others acceptable, it undermines anything else you have to say because it comes off as nothing but pedantic+menial.

Yeah it just felt like a TV movie and not like the Hooper version which is actually pretty cinematic (shot on film with an old pro like James Mason) but like a cheap USA TV movie from the 90 s or 00s . I agree the Flanagan influence isn't helping.

I mean, the beauty of the novel is that it’s a small town drama that has horror elements parachuted into it. It takes its time, it’s about getting to know these characters, getting to know and understand the setting; and that gives weight to the supernatural stuff, gives meaning to the consequences. That’s King’s secret more than anything. He writes characters first and foremost. 

A film of that book was always on a hiding to nothing for that reason. How can you cram all of that into a film? You either narrow the scope so much it’s about a single character (in which case, why make Salem’s Lot? It’s about the town. It’s literally in the name), or you rush it trying to get a semblance of everything in, and end up with a crude outline of the story drawn in crayon, a kinda cliff notes version. 

It really should have been a mini-series, and it really should have had Mike Flanagan in charge of it, but he basically did exactly that in all but name with Midnight Mass.
That’s just standard criticism though. You are being oversensitive.

It's yet another indictment of our age that even with an open goal like 'Salem's Lot', a modern director and production team will find a way to make a complete and utter mess of it.

All the hard work has been done for them. The story, the characters, the plot, the setting, the legacy of a much-loved cultural touchstone is all there and handed to them on a plate and yet they fail to exercise the smallest modicum of imagination in bringing it to life for a new generation. Like, how could you possibly fuck this up???

Cluelessly untalented people.

It's kind of you to consider giving feedback, but I would never encourage a critic with no ethos. Does this kind of review even belong in this sub? It's a bit of a stretch to say they are inviting any discussion about the film itself.

TBF this is a Stephen King adaptation. 4/5 times it's gonna mediocre, but King works print money so they'll always be made.
I'm not gonna defend this production because I haven't seen the movie (nor do I want to). But can you really call it a modern issue? Hollywood has been making hollow adaptations since forever.

Oh so it's ok if [scott tobias called Alejandro González Iñárritu a pretentious fraud!](https://thedissolve.com/reviews/1152-birdman/), but if an amateur like me writes something like that, I'm not going to be taken seriously
You’re missing the entire point then - and I don’t engage further in a [whataboutisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whataboutism).

Compare this to the remake of say, 'Invasion of the Bodysnatchers' - this was given a new lease of life and made much darker and arguably even gives the original a run for it's money. The team behind it re-interpreted the whole concept and delivered something even more mysterious and memorable. 

Too often, modern-day remakes are toothless, use post-modern irony as a crutch and don't seek to engage or connect with the viewer on any deep level, lack imagination and are competent unmemorable.

I see what you’re saying but what about panned remakes today? Dune for instance was very well received in comparison to Lynch’s 1985 version. For that matter, what about the countless shitty remakes in 1978? Watch Bad News Bears go to Japan and tell me it isn’t hot garbage. History forgets the dirt because the diamonds are the only ones that retain their shine.   
  
It’s easy to bash modern movies because more of it is bad than less, but that’s always how it’s been. The quantity has just gone up because we are flooded with streaming companies competing with Hollywood. Honestly this is a good thing for visionary artists like Del Toro or Flannigan or Langthimos or Scorsese who are so creative and excellent at their style of directing they don’t require financial or studio pressure to make great art. OTOH those lags in pressure can be negative on some, like the Russo Brothers, M. Night Shyamalan, or Danny Boyle.  
  
I tend to think similarly to you in respects to modern films, but if you are more selective in what you watch, you can sift through the plethora of content and still find gold.
